subject: Onramp orchestration & transfer-of-responsibility timeline (post-signature)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@auramark.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@auramark.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 15:28:00 -0800
Subject: Onramp orchestration & transfer-of-responsibility timeline (post-signature)

Hi Samir / Priya —

Congrats again on finalizing the commercial terms. Attached is a draft onramp plan I promised — a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature execution rhythm (rollout windows, canary, migration, and training). High level summary below and explicit asks at the end.

Key dates (provisional, assuming SOW signed 2027-11-10):
- Week 0 (2027-11-10): Contract countersign (target).
- Week 1–2 (2027-11-13 to 2027-11-24): Environment provisioning + initial networking checks (VPC peering, firewall rules).
- Week 3 (2027-11-27 to 2027-11-30): Canary week — traffic shadowing to Redwood Dedicated nodes (1% production equivalent), validation against evaluation suite.
- Week 4 (2027-12-04 to 2027-12-08): Data migration window (bulk import + verification), fallback readiness.
- Week 5–6 (2027-12-11 to 2027-12-22): Staged cutover (50% -> 100%) and training sessions for ops and app teams.

Evaluation plan (short):
- We will run the supplied evaluation set (attached) during the canary window: latency percentiles (p50/p95), token-cost delta, and top-3 semantic fidelity checks.
- Acceptance gates: p95 latency within 1.3x baseline, production request error rate < 0.5%, and no regressions on 5 critical prompts.

Rollout cadence & responsibilities (from the MAP worksheet):
- Redwood: cluster provisioning, canary orchestration, rollback policy, runbooks. (Primary: Marcus)
- Auramark: approve firewall/IP allowlist, provide canonical eval prompt set, finalize production cutover owner and calendar. (Primary: Samir / Priya)
- Joint: weekly standups during onramp, post-mortem after canary.

Attachments: Auramark_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + responsibilities), SOW-draft.pdf (commercial redline).

Asks today:
1) Confirm SOW sign target (I used 2027-11-10 in the plan).
2) Share the canonical eval set by 2027-11-15 (we can ingest and run it during canary).
3) Confirm a primary app owner for cutover (name + email) so we can list them in the MAP and in Pager duty handoffs.

If these dates look tight, tell me which milestone to shift and we’ll re-sequence. Happy to run a 30-min walk-through of the MAP tomorrow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0127

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@auramark.com>

Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@auramark.com>, Ben Sawyer <bsawyer@auramark.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 09:12:43 -0800
Subject: Re: Onramp orchestration & transfer-of-responsibility timeline (post-signature)

Thanks Marcus — this looks comprehensive and appreciated. A few quick notes from our side after an internal sync: 

- SOW sign target: We’re aligned for 2027-11-10 but procurement may ask for a 48-hour review of the final SOW; please expect a hold until 2027-11-12 in the worst case.
- Eval set: Priya will drop the initial 150 prompts by 2027-11-12; we expect you to run the canary evaluation against this corpus.
- Canary scope: Can you confirm what "1% production equivalent" means for us? Our traffic is bursty; we want to ensure the canary simulates the 99th percentile burst.

On acceptance gates: the latency threshold looks fair; one additional ask — can we add an availability probe during canary that exercises the fallback path (e.g., dark routing to fallback model) so we can validate graceful degradation?

We also want a 90-minute runbook review before the migration window (ideally 2027-12-01).

If you can confirm the canary load shape and schedule the runbook review, we’ll lock the internal calendar.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of AI Ops, Auramark
samir.patel@auramark.com | +1 617-555-0874

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Onramp orchestration & transfer-of-responsibility timeline (post-signature)

Marcus / Jonas —

Quick internal coordination. Action items I’ll take on and asks for Jonas: 
1) Training curriculum draft for Auramark ops (2 x 60-minute sessions: "SLOs & incident playbook" and "Model management & quant profiles"). I’ll build the slides — target delivery 2027-11-22.
2) Canary load shaping: Jonas — can you prepare a load script that includes a 30s spike to simulate 99th percentile bursts and a baseline steady stream? We’ll run this during the canary week. Ideally the script can be toggled for token-length distributions (short vs. long prompts).
3) Runbook review: I propose 2027-12-01 09:00 PT for the 90-minute session; Marcus — please confirm with Samir.

I’ll also update the MAP spreadsheet with training owners and attach a separate training-schedule.csv before the week of 11/22.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@auramark.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@auramark.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Sawyer <bsawyer@auramark.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onramp orchestration & transfer-of-responsibility timeline (post-signature)

Thanks all — quick update and confirmations: 

- SOW sign: Understood re: procurement review; we’ll mark 2027-11-12 as contingency in the MAP.
- Canary load shape: Jonas (cc’d) will provide a load script that includes both baseline steady-state and a 30s spike to emulate p99 bursts. The 1% figure is an attempt to limit real user impact; operationally we’ll run the script against the dedicated canary cluster with parallel shadow traffic to the production model to validate fidelity. We’ll send the load script and a short runbook on 2027-11-19.
- Availability probe + fallback: Agreed — we’ll add a synthetic probe that triggers the fallback routing and validates the graceful degradation path during canary. Acceptance gate updated to include the probe success metric.
- Runbook review is confirmed for 2027-12-01 09:00 PT (90 mins) — invite to follow.

Next steps I’ll own: update the attached MAP with contingency dates and the updated acceptance gates, circulate final_MAP_v1.xlsx, and drop a training-schedule.csv with session owners by 2027-11-22.

Samir / Priya — if you can confirm the primary cutover owner (name / mobile) by EOD 2027-11-12 we’ll populate the escalation table.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
